0.long_answer: Propionic acidemia is an autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency of the enzyme propionyl-CoA carboxylase. This deficiency disrupts the conversion of propionyl-CoA to methylmalonyl-CoA, leading to the buildup of toxic substrates, metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia, and ketotic hyperglycinemia. The ketotic hyperglycinemia observed is a distinguishing feature that sets propionic acidemia apart from glycine encephalopathy, where the primary issue is the defective metabolism of glycine without the additional metabolic disturbances seen in propionic acidemia.
